name: Wu Xiaoliin
profile: Listed on Hurun China 2021 (US$310m) with source of wealth 'Link' (chemical products). Searches could not tie 吴晓林 to a specific company; the likely candidate, Lianhe Chemical Technology (联化科技, 002250.SZ), is chaired by Wang Ping and its public shareholder/executive lists do not show this name.
notes: Identity unresolved: 'Link' company not identified. Do not confuse with a different Wu Xiaolin (b.1981) named on a Hong Kong SFC persons-of-interest list. Needs Hurun original entry to resolve.

name: Ni Weiju
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (with husband Ye Dalin), Zhejiang Tailin Bioengineering Co. (300813.SZ)
profile: Ni Weiju (倪卫菊) and her husband Ye Dalin are the controlling shareholders and actual controllers of Hangzhou-based Zhejiang Tailin Bioengineering, a Shenzhen ChiNext-listed maker of microbial testing, organic-matter analysis and contamination-control instruments for pharma labs. The couple control ~57% of the company; in 2025 Ye transferred a ~10% block to Ni (she now holds ~15%).
interesting_fact: In June 2025 Ye Dalin transferred 12.1m Tailin shares (~10% of the company) to Ni Weiju as an internal spousal adjustment, leaving their combined ~57% control unchanged.
notes: Low public profile; no executive title confirmed for her. Emails are the board-secretary / securities-affairs rep contacts published in Tailin's 2024 interim report (verify against latest report). Husband Ye Dalin is the public face.

name: Lu Sanping
current_role: Co-founder and shareholder (no executive role), Broad-Ocean Motor / Zhongshan Dayang Electric (002249.SZ)
profile: Lu Sanping (鲁三平) is one of the six founding promoters of Zhongshan Broad-Ocean Motor (大洋电机), the Guangdong maker of micro-motors, HVAC motors and EV drive systems chaired by his elder brother Lu Chuping. A passive shareholder holding no company post, he sold down his stake from above 5% in 2016-2018 and held ~1.4% by 2019.
interesting_fact: Broad-Ocean's articles of association list Lu Sanping among the company's six original promoters alongside his brother Lu Chuping, who has chaired the motor maker since 2000.
notes: Very low profile; 2016 filing states he holds no position at the company. Company IR emails (from 2020 interim report) are the only route; brother Lu Chuping is the public face. Not on Hurun since 2016.

name: Sir John Ritblat
current_role: Honorary President, The British Land Company PLC (former chairman & CEO)
profile: Sir John Ritblat (b. 1935, Hampstead) bought British Land from Jim Slater in 1970 for £1m and built it into one of the UK's largest REITs, chairing it until 2006. Now 91, he is honorary president of British Land and has chaired Colliers CRE and the advisory board of Delancey, the property investor founded by his son Jamie.
interesting_fact: He acquired British Land from financier Jim Slater in 1970 for just £1m and ran it for 36 years before retiring as chairman in 2006.
deep_cut_fact: The British Library's permanent treasures gallery (Magna Carta, Lindisfarne Gospels, Shakespeare First Folio) is the Sir John Ritblat Gallery, named for him after he gave £1m toward its display cases; he is also honorary president of the British Ski and Snowboard Federation.
notes: Aged 91, largely retired; no personal published contacts found. Possible indirect routes: British Land corporate/press office or Delancey (son's firm), but neither is his personal office. Wikipedia cites the BSSF role without a source; gallery fact is well documented.

name: Wang Panrong
current_role: Former co-controlling shareholder of SEC Electric Machinery (中电电机, 603988.SH); no current role confirmed
profile: Wang Panrong (王盘荣) was one of the actual controllers, with Wang Jianyu and Wang Jiankai, of Wuxi-based SEC Electric Machinery, a maker of large and medium AC/DC motors and generators listed in Shanghai in 2014. In 2024 the Wang family's holding vehicle sold 30% to Beijing Gaodi Resources, handing control to gold-mining entrepreneur Guo Wenjun (completed Dec 2024).
interesting_fact: In 2024 the founding Wang family sold control of SEC Electric Machinery to Beijing Gaodi Resources, making a gold-mine owner the motor maker's new actual controller; Wang Panrong was a party to the supplementary deal agreement.
notes: Very low profile; no longer tied to the company after the 2024 control change. IPO prospectus naming him as actual controller: https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN201409110006968502_1.PDF. No usable contact route found.

name: Terence Cole
profile: Terence Cole (1933-2022), co-founder with Mark Steinberg in 1976 of MARCOL, the London-based international property investment group (owner of Chelsea Harbour from 2003). Died December 2022 per a tribute in Finito World quoting MARCOL co-founder Mark Steinberg.
notes: Deceased (December 2022). Source: https://finitoworld.com/?p=4037 (tribute 'An Indelible Mark: Terence Cole: 1933-2022'). Rest skipped per instructions; MARCOL continues under Mark Steinberg.

name: Wendell P Weeks
current_role: Chairman, CEO and President, Corning Incorporated; director, Amazon.com
profile: Wendell Weeks joined Corning in finance in 1983, ran its optical-fiber business from 1996, became CEO in 2005, chairman in 2007 and also president in Oct 2025. His wealth comes from Corning equity. Corning is now a key AI data-center supplier: in Jan 2026 it signed a multiyear deal of up to $6bn to supply Meta's US data-center buildout with fiber and connectivity.
interesting_fact: Steve Jobs called Weeks about six months before the 2007 iPhone launch; that led Corning to revive Gorilla Glass, a strengthened glass it had shelved for decades. Weeks will receive Yale's Legend in Leadership Award in Sept 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Despite starting in Corning's finance division (Lehigh BA, Harvard MBA Baker Scholar), Weeks is a named inventor on some 47 U.S. patents, including pharmaceutical glass vials that resist delamination and curved automotive interior display covers.
notes: Strong fit for a data-center podcast (optical fiber for AI, Meta deal). Media contacts rotate by release; use the latest Corning release. Patent count varies by Corning page (44 vs 47).

name: the Gosling family
profile: A family entry (Sunday Times Rich List 2020, inheritance, ~£200m) likely corresponding to the heirs of Sir Donald Gosling (1929-2019), co-founder of National Car Parks, who started with a £200 car park on a Holborn bombsite after WWII and retired as NCP co-chairman in 1998. This link could not be confirmed from the list itself, and the co-listed 'Gabriella di Nora' could not be identified.
interesting_fact: Sir Donald Gosling and Ronald Hobson built National Car Parks from a £200 investment in a bombed-out Holborn site; in 1998 Gosling took his yacht Leander G to meet submarine HMS Splendid during the Kosovo War so its crew could rest and shower.
notes: Family entry, not an individual; identity of the family unconfirmed (assumed Sir Donald Gosling's heirs, who are private individuals). No public contact route. Probably not a fit for outreach.

name: Ronald David Miller
current_role: Co-Founder & Chairman of the Board, StartEngine Crowdfunding, Inc. (STGC)
profile: Ron Miller is a lawyer-turned-serial entrepreneur who founded, built and sold five companies (including Disability Group, Inc., a large Social Security disability advocacy firm) before joining Howard Marks in 2014 to turn StartEngine from an accelerator into an equity-crowdfunding portal. He chairs StartEngine and, via his trust, holds tens of millions of its shares.
interesting_fact: A four-time Inc. 500/5000 honoree and EY Entrepreneur of the Year finalist, Miller founded the San Diego chapter of the Entrepreneurs' Organization (EO) and served on the YPO/WPO executive committee.
deep_cut_fact: He sits on the board of West Coast Care, a nonprofit helping homeless individuals get off the street, and advises USC's Greif Center for Entrepreneurial Studies.
notes: Good fit for an entrepreneurship/fundraising angle. Only company general contact found; no personal published contact. Disability Group detail comes from aggregator profiles (village.ai), not primary.

name: Adam D Goldstein
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Chairman, Archer Aviation Inc. (NYSE: ACHR)
profile: Adam Goldstein spent years as an investment analyst/portfolio manager, then co-founded recruiting marketplace Vettery (2012), sold to Adecco in 2018 for a reported ~$100m. In 2018 he co-founded Archer Aviation, the eVTOL 'air taxi' developer (Midnight aircraft) that listed via SPAC in 2021; he has been sole CEO since April 2022 and is pursuing launches in the UAE and US.
interesting_fact: Vettery raised a $9m round in 2016 with a deck of just nine slides while the startup had 25 people (Business Insider); Adecco bought it two years later.
deep_cut_fact: He has sat on the Board of Trustees of the Museum of American Finance (Wall Street, NYC) since 2013, and early in his career was a senior analyst at Cedar Hill Capital Partners (2005-2009).
notes: Frequent conference speaker (Milken, US Chamber Aerospace Summit, Dubai Airshow) - media-friendly. Press email not verified (web search budget ran out); check the media contact on Archer's latest Business Wire release.

name: Matthew J Meloy
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and Director, Targa Resources Corp. (NYSE: TRGP)
profile: Matt Meloy has led Houston-based midstream giant Targa Resources as CEO since March 2020, after serving as its CFO (2010-2018) and President (2018-2020). Targa gathers, processes and transports natural gas and NGLs, largely in the Permian; in Q3 2026 it posted record Permian volumes and $1.5bn adjusted EBITDA and signed 20-year agreements with ExxonMobil backed by three new Delaware Basin gas plants.
interesting_fact: In August 2026 Targa announced 20-year fee-based midstream agreements with ExxonMobil subsidiaries in the Permian and three new processing plants ('Wrangler', 'Ranger' and 'Ranger II') to serve them.
deep_cut_fact: Meloy joined Targa in March 2006 as Director of Corporate Development after about two and a half years in Royal Bank of Scotland's energy structured-finance group, and rose through treasurer and CFO roles to CEO in 14 years.
notes: Strong fit for energy angle (Permian gas supply, which feeds power for data centers). Targa website blocks automated fetches; IR email is from the Q3 2026 earnings release.

name: Elliott Bernerd
current_role: Co-founder and chairman, Chelsfield (London property investment group) - current title not re-verified
profile: Elliott Bernerd (b. 1945, Maida Vale) left school at 15 to work for Dorrington Investment Trust and became one of London's best-known property dealers. He developed Stockley Park, co-founded Chelsfield in 1986 with Stuart Lipton, and made landmark deals including Wentworth Golf Club, Merry Hill shopping centre and Camden Market; Qatar's QIA bought 20% of Chelsfield in 2008.
interesting_fact: He bought the Stockley Park site in west London for £8m in 1983; the development sold for £365m in 1988. Chelsfield also bought Wentworth Golf Club for about £17.7m in 1988.
deep_cut_fact: A serious classical-music patron, Bernerd was a trustee of the London Philharmonic Orchestra and in 1993 publicly fought Arts Council plans to cut funding to London orchestras, saying the jobs of 250 LPO musicians were at stake.
notes: Private; aged 81. No published personal or office contact found (web search budget exhausted before checking Chelsfield's current site). Avoid the La Hougue offshore-trust and 1992 Mellor-flat stories.

name: Hemant Kanoria
current_role: Founder and former Chairman & MD, Srei Infrastructure Finance; founder, Kanoria Foundation
profile: Kolkata entrepreneur Hemant Kanoria ran two family flour mills in West Bengal before founding, with brother Sunil Kanoria, Srei - an infrastructure and construction-equipment financier that became one of India's largest NBFCs in its sector. Srei's board was superseded by the RBI in 2021 and the companies went through insolvency resolution; Kanoria remains active in philanthropy.
interesting_fact: Before Srei he operated two family-owned flour mills in West Bengal, then pivoted into financing construction equipment for India's infrastructure build-out; he later chaired FICCI's National Committee on Infrastructure.
deep_cut_fact: In 2014 he set up the Kanoria Foundation, which runs Suryodaya schools for underprivileged children and created the Acid Survivors and Women Welfare Foundation for treatment and rehabilitation of acid-attack survivors.
notes: Sensitive: Srei was taken over by RBI in 2021 and went through IBC insolvency - avoid as outreach topic. No published contact found; Kanoria Foundation would be the most appropriate route (site not verified). Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemant_Kanoria

name: John G Morikis
current_role: Retired Sherwin-Williams CEO/Executive Chair; independent director of UPS, Johnson & Johnson, General Mills and Whirlpool
profile: John Morikis (62) spent 40 years at Sherwin-Williams, starting in sales in 1984, running Paint Stores (1999-2006), serving as President & COO (2006-2016), CEO (2016-2023), chair (2017-2023) and Executive Chair (2024); he left the board in April 2025. He led the $11.3bn Valspar acquisition and now sits on the boards of UPS, J&J, General Mills and Whirlpool.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Sherwin-Williams expanded to 123 countries, closed an $11.3bn international coatings acquisition (Valspar) and posted 13 consecutive years of sales growth.
deep_cut_fact: He championed customer tech at Sherwin-Williams including a colour-capture mobile app and a first-of-its-kind microbicidal paint; he holds a B.A. in business administration and psychology from Saint Joseph's College and an MBA from National Louis University.
notes: No longer an executive at Sherwin-Williams (input title outdated). No personal published contact; reachable only via board/company corporate secretaries. SHW proxy confirming retirement from its board: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/89800/000008980026000025/shw-20260310.htm

name: Ian T Lowitt
current_role: Group Chief Executive Officer and Director, Marex Group (Nasdaq: MRX)
profile: Ian Lowitt joined London-based commodities and financial-services broker Marex as CFO in 2012 and has been CEO since January 2016, taking it public on Nasdaq in 2024. Before that he spent 1994-2008 at Lehman Brothers (strategy, treasury, CFO) and 2008-2012 at Barclays. Marex reported record Q3 2026 results, with $495m adjusted profit before tax for the first nine months.
interesting_fact: Under Lowitt, Marex has grown through acquisitions into a diversified clearing, energy/commodities brokerage and market-making group, reporting record revenue and adjusted PBT of $176m in Q3 2026 and targeting 10-20% annual profit growth.
deep_cut_fact: Lowitt trained as an electrical engineer, earning BSc and MSc degrees in electrical engineering at Wits University in Johannesburg, before going to Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar (MA in PPE, MSc in Economics).
notes: Good fit for energy-markets angle (Marex is a major energy/commodities broker). Avoid dwelling on his Lehman CFO tenure in 2008.
